newsitem.title: UK: Croatia rated at investment grade by IBCA and S&P.
newsitem.headline: Croatia rated at investment grade by IBCA and S&P.

text.p: Croatia was awarded investment grade credit ratings by two major ratings agencies on Friday.

Standard & Poor's, the U.S. rating agency, and IBCA, its European counterpart, both assigned BBB minus ratings to Croatia's long-term foreign currency debt, recognising the country's efforts to stabilise its economy.
But the agencies said Croatia faced some hurdles.
"Croatia's ratings depend on continued adherence to conservative fiscal policies and progress in restructuring the banking and corporate sectors," S&P said.
"Maintaining low inflation, sustaining output growth and reviving employment, are the key economic challenges."
Long-term local currency debt ratings of A minus were also awarded to the country, while short-term local currency obligations were rated A2 by S&P and A3 by IBCA.

IBCA said the investment grade sovereign rating reflected Croatia's impressive macro-economic stabilisation, its rate of inflation -- the lowest of the transition economies -- and its substantial export-earning capacity and potential.
"The lack of a track record of national institutions is a constraint on the rating, but is less so than in other countries emerging from federations," IBCA said.

"War and the need to defend the fledgling state have been an exceptional spur to institution-building, and the Croatians have been able to draw on financial and other help from members of the Croatian diaspora," it added.
